mutations.because: the confinement check is skipped: a ref `resolveAssetPath` refuses is handed to the parser as though it had passed. `/etc/passwd` then parses to no campaign and answers ENOENT rather than undefined, and `../outside.png` parses the same way — so a run over a brief naming a path outside the assets tree fails loudly where fs skipped the asset cleanly, and a brief naming `/etc/passwd` gets an error naming an asset rather than being ignored. The confinement decision is the ONE thing this port must not make twice: it is made once, in `resolveAssetPath`, so the object port's refusals and `FileSystemInputAssets`' cannot drift apart.

the memo starts remembering failures, as an empty read rather than as an absence. The run that is waiting on an upload is the case that dies: the preview that ran before the upload, the re-run after it, and every retry in between all get the cached zero-length answer and report a missing logo for the rest of the reader's life — while the store has held the right bytes the whole time. Caching only SUCCESSFUL reads is the whole of the memo's contract; a cache that remembers a refusal is a cache that lies, and the retry test (a MISSING ref, then the upload, then the read) is the only case that can see it, because every other test reads once.
